title: Train for the decisions people make with AI tools
summary: Plan practice that checks how employees use AI assistance, verify suggested answers and decide when to revise, reject or escalate a recommendation.
body_markdown:
When an AI assistant suggests a response or next action, the employee still has to decide whether it fits the situation. Prepare people to use that help within a real task, including recognizing when the suggestion is incomplete, inappropriate or unsupported.


## Define the human responsibility


Choose a specific workflow before teaching prompting techniques. For a support representative, that might mean understanding a billing request, asking an approved assistant for relevant guidance and deciding what to communicate. Describe which decisions remain with the employee, which actions require approval and what information may be shared with the tool.


A well-written prompt is only one part of the task. The person also needs to identify missing context, check the response against approved information and notice when the tool cannot provide a reliable answer. Assess those behaviors alongside the quality of the request they give the assistant.


## Keep practice aligned with the assisted workflow


Practice should reflect the assistance employees are allowed to use at work. If a training environment cannot reproduce that assistance, explain the limitation and decide which part of the task it can meaningfully assess. Do not interpret a result from an unassisted exercise as proof that someone can use a copilot safely, or assume that a convincing demonstration covers your internal tool.


## Build an AI-assisted task check


Use this worksheet with your training and operations owners. Test both a useful suggestion and one that needs correction, using fictional information and approved testing arrangements.


Step Observable behavior


Understand the request Identify the customer's need and information still missing


Ask for assistance Give relevant context without sharing prohibited information


Check the response Compare material claims with the approved source or procedure


Choose an action Accept, revise, reject or escalate the suggestion with a reason


Complete the task Explain the outcome and record what the workflow requires


## A fictional example: a suggested billing response


A customer asks why a promotional price disappeared from an invoice. An assistant drafts a confident response using an expired offer. In practice, the representative must check the offer dates, identify the mismatch and use the current billing policy before replying. A second attempt includes missing account information, so the appropriate next step is to ask a clarifying question. The trainer reviews the representative's reasoning and final action, rather than rewarding fluent prompting or accepting the assistant's wording as the correct answer.


## Review the workflow when the tool changes


Record which assistance was available during an assessment and which version of the procedure it used. If the tool's permissions, guidance or place in the workflow changes, revisit the exercise and its expected behavior. An employee should not be assessed against a process that no longer matches the job.


Keep workforce training separate from technical evaluation of the AI system. Training can examine how people use assistance; it does not establish the tool's accuracy or authorize its deployment. Before choosing a simulation platform, ask to test the specific assisted task and confirm what is represented, what is simplified and what remains outside scope. Use that evidence to decide whether the exercise supports your training objective.
